title: Narcissism test: how strong are your narcissistic traits? — cv.cm
description: Free narcissism test: rate 16 statements on admiration, entitlement and empathy to get a score from 0 to 64. It measures a personality trait and can't diagnose anyone. Answers stay in your browser.
lede: Am I a narcissist? Rate 16 honest statements about attention, status and empathy to see where you fall on the narcissism scale, and what your score does and doesn't mean.
about: Narcissism is a personality trait that everyone has to some degree. It runs from healthy self-confidence to a strong need for admiration, a sense of entitlement and little interest in other people's feelings. Psychologists have measured it since Raskin and Hall's Narcissistic Personality Inventory in 1979.

The statements here were written for cv.cm and are not a clinical instrument. Half are reversed, so agreeing with everything doesn't raise your score. Narcissistic personality disorder is a rare condition that only a qualified professional can diagnose, and a high score here doesn't mean you have it. This test is about you: it isn't meant for labeling a partner, a parent or anybody else.

faq.q: Can this test tell me whether I'm a narcissist?
faq.a: It shows how strongly you recognize some narcissistic traits in yourself. It can't diagnose narcissistic personality disorder, which needs a professional assessment of long-standing patterns and the harm they cause.

faq.q: How is the score worked out?
faq.a: Each statement scores 0 to 4, half reversed, so the total runs from 0 to 64. 21 or less is low, 22 to 42 is medium, and 43 or more is high. The bands are a guide for this test, not clinical cut-offs.
Yes. Confidence, ambition and enjoying recognition are normal. Problems start when the need for admiration comes at other people's expense or when any criticism feels unbearable.

faq.q: What if someone close to me behaves like a narcissist?
faq.a: A quiz taken on someone else's behalf can't tell you much. Focus on the behavior and how it affects you. If you feel controlled, belittled or unsafe, talk to someone you trust, a counselor or a local support service.

items: I like being the center of attention.
I feel uncomfortable when people praise me.
I deserve more recognition than I usually get.
I don't expect special treatment from anybody.
Deep down, I know I'm better than most people.
I think most people are about as capable as I am.
When someone criticizes me, I get angry or look for a way to hit back.
I can take criticism without feeling attacked.
Other people's problems often bore me.
I go out of my way to understand how others feel.
Rules are for other people; I should be able to bend them.
I'm happy to wait my turn like everybody else.
I often use charm to get what I want from people.
I'm happy to let others take the credit.
I need people to admire me to feel good about myself.
I feel fine about myself even when nobody notices what I do.

low.name: Few narcissistic traits (0–21)
low.body: You don't seem to need much admiration and you make room for other people. If your score is very low, check that you aren't underselling yourself: it's fine to take credit for good work and ask for what you need.

mid.name: Some narcissistic traits (22–42)
mid.body: You have an ordinary mix: some confidence and a liking for recognition, along with an interest in others. Watch which situations bring out the more self-centered side, such as criticism or competition.

high.name: Strong narcissistic traits (43–64)
high.body: You recognize many narcissistic traits in yourself, like a strong need for admiration and sensitivity to criticism. This is not a diagnosis. It can help to ask people you trust how you come across, practice listening and, if this causes trouble in your relationships or work, talk to a therapist.
